text: It is the most valuable word in patient advocacy. And the most abused. I'm the founder of the Cold Ischemia Foundation, and I'm going to show you, with receipts, who really pays for the voices that claim to speak for patients.

In 2017, researchers at the University of Pennsylvania examined the hundred and four largest patient advocacy groups in America. Eighty-three percent took money from drug, device, or biotech companies. More than a third had an industry executive on the board. And only one, one, said plainly that it takes no industry money.
src: McCoy et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 2017

text: In a single year, drugmakers gave a hundred and sixteen million dollars to five hundred ninety-four patient groups. Nobody was required to tell you.

In 2018, DaVita and Fresenius, the two largest dialysis companies in America, gave the American Kidney Fund about two hundred forty-seven million dollars. An independent audit put that at roughly eighty percent of its donor base. A former employee sued, alleging aid was steered toward the donors' patients. The Justice Department declined to join, and the case was dismissed. In 2023, DaVita disclosed that the District of Columbia attorney general had demanded its communications with the Fund.
src: The American Prospect, 2019 · Bloomberg, 2019 · STAT, 2023 · DaVita SEC filing

text: Dialysis Patient Citizens was born in 2004 from a DaVita grant. Its original name: DaVita Patient Citizens. When California capped what dialysis companies could bill for charity-assisted patients, the American Kidney Fund and Dialysis Patient Citizens sued to block the law. The industry spent two hundred thirty-three million dollars on California campaigns in four years. And DaVita has resolved kickback allegations with the Justice Department three times in a decade, including three hundred fifty million dollars in 2014.
src: DPC funding fact sheet · Healio, 2020 · KFF Health News, 2020 · U.S. Dept. of Justice, 2014

text: The National Kidney Foundation lists Boehringer Ingelheim, Novo Nordisk and Vertex as platinum corporate members. The American Association of Kidney Patients lists Amgen, AstraZeneca, Baxter, Bayer, DaVita and Fresenius as partners. The Caregiver Action Network's leadership council includes Pfizer, Astellas, Eisai and Teva.
src: Each organization's own corporate membership pages

text: Senate investigators found drugmakers gave the National Alliance on Mental Illness nearly twenty-three million dollars in three years, about three-quarters of its donations. The Alliance for Patient Access took more than one-point-eight million from the drug lobby PhRMA, and its executive director ran a Washington lobbying firm. Patients Rising. The American Diabetes Association. Even the American Heart Association, which, to its credit, publishes the number: five percent.
src: U.S. Senate Finance Committee, 2009 · Associated Press · KFF Health News · American Heart Association

text: All of this is in their own filings and on their own pages. Taking this money is legal, and many of these groups do real work. But when did any of them last name a funder's prices, profits, or settlements?

We take no donations. No grants. No sponsors. No money from drugmakers, dialysis companies, hospitals, or insurers. We charge fees only for work you ask us to do. That is not a slogan. It is a structure. When no one pays for your voice, nothing is off limits.
Don't trust me. Check every number. Read their filings. Then ask one question. Who pays for the voice that speaks for the patient? Independent is not what you call yourself. It is what you can prove.
